# Luxora Objection Handling Guide

## “I need to talk to my partner/spouse/business partner.”

“Absolutely. Let’s get them on a quick call so everyone hears the same information directly.

Usually when owners wait a few days and try to explain everything later, momentum dies and important details get lost.

What’s their email? Let’s lock in a time now while this is fresh.”

---

## “I’m in a transition right now.”

“That’s actually why now is the right time.

If we wait until after the move, expansion, or hiring phase, you’ll already be overwhelmed trying to fix systems while operating in chaos.

The goal is to have memberships, packages, follow-up, retention, and marketing already dialed in before the next phase launches.

The owners who scale the fastest prepare before the growth happens, not after.”

---

## “I already have someone handling marketing.”

“Perfect. We’re not replacing them unless you want us to.

Marketing is only one piece of what we do. Most med spas are leaking money after the lead comes in.

We fix:
• Consult conversions
• Memberships
• Packages
• Retention
• Follow-up
• Client experience
• Revenue per client

If your marketing is already working, this usually makes your current results perform even better.”

---

## “How are you different from everyone else?”

“Most agencies sell leads and keep you dependent.

We build the actual systems inside the business that create long-term revenue:
• Memberships
• Packages
• Retention
• Follow-up
• Front desk conversions
• Lifetime client value

And we move fast.

Most owners come to us after wasting 6 to 12 months with agencies that gave them reports instead of results.

Our goal is simple: fix the leaks, increase revenue, and build systems your team can actually sustain.”

---

## “Pricing feels high.”

“I completely understand. But most owners are already losing far more than this every single month in missed revenue.

One weak membership system, poor follow-up process, or undertrained consult flow can cost a practice tens of thousands monthly.

That’s why we focus on ROI immediately.

Most clients recover the investment quickly through better retention, memberships, packages, and reactivating existing clients alone.

The bigger risk honestly is staying stuck for another 6 to 12 months.”

---

## “Let me think about it.”

“Of course. Usually when someone says that, it comes down to one thing:
• Timing
• Money
• Trust
• Fear of another bad experience

Which one feels most true for you?

I’d rather address it directly now than let you walk away still unsure.

And honestly, the owners who move the fastest usually see the biggest wins because they stop sitting in decision paralysis and start fixing the problems.”
I’ll focus this on strengthening the pitch/close language, especially where these objection handles connect to the pitch, temperature check, price drop, and post-price silence.

These are solid conceptually, but a few of them are too long, too explanatory, and slightly defensive. The strongest objection handling in this framework is:

- Calm
- Direct
- Short
- Based on THEIR discovery answers
- Ends with a question that reopens the sale

Right now a few of these sound like mini-monologues. You want more control and less “convincing.” fileciteturn1file6L1-L40

Here’s the tightened version:

---

## “I need to talk to my partner/spouse/business partner.”

“Totally fair.

Just so I understand — is that because they’re financially involved in the decision, or because you want their opinion before moving forward?”

[Let them answer]

“Got it. Usually what happens when owners leave a call and try to relay everything later, important context gets lost and momentum dies.

Let’s just get them on a quick call so everyone can hear the same information directly.

What’s the best way to coordinate that?”

---

## “I’m in a transition right now.”

“That’s usually why now becomes the right time.

If you wait until after the expansion, move, hiring phase, or growth push, you’re trying to fix systems while operating in chaos.

Right now we can get the memberships, retention, follow-up, and conversion systems dialed in before things get busier.

The owners who scale the cleanest prepare before growth hits, not after it becomes painful.”

---

## “I already have someone handling marketing.”

“Perfect. We’re not trying to replace what’s already working.

Most med spas actually don’t have a lead problem — they have a conversion, retention, and follow-up problem after the lead comes in.

That’s why we focus heavily on:
• Memberships
• Packages
• Follow-up
• Consult conversions
• Retention
• Revenue per client

So if your marketing is already producing leads, this usually just helps you monetize those leads better.”

---

## “How are you different from everyone else?”

“Most agencies stop at lead generation.

We focus on the systems inside the business that actually increase revenue long term:
• Memberships
• Retention
• Packages
• Follow-up
• Front desk conversion
• Lifetime client value

A lot of owners come to us after spending months with agencies that generated activity but didn’t improve the business itself.

Our goal is simple:
Fix the leaks, increase client value, and build systems your team can realistically sustain.”

---

## “Pricing feels high.”

“I hear you.

But based on what you shared earlier, the cost of staying where you are is probably already far higher than the investment itself.

Weak follow-up, poor retention, low consult conversion, and underdeveloped memberships quietly cost practices a lot of revenue every month.

That’s why our focus is ROI first.

The goal isn’t to ‘buy marketing.’
The goal is to recover lost revenue and create more predictable cash flow.”

---

## “Let me think about it.”

“Of course.

Usually when someone says that, there’s still something unresolved underneath it.

Typically it comes down to:
• Timing
• Money
• Trust
• Fear of making the wrong decision

Which one feels most true for you?”

[Let them answer]

“I’d rather address it directly than have you leave the call still uncertain.”

---

Big improvement opportunity:
Start tying objections back to THEIR words from discovery.

Example:

“Earlier you mentioned your retention is inconsistent and your follow-up is almost nonexistent…”

That immediately makes the objection handling feel personalized instead of scripted. That’s the standard the framework pushes heavily. fileciteturn1file6L41-L120

Your objection handles are strong, but they should **not live inside the pitch**. The pitch should create buy-in first; objections after price should loop back to discovery, not become brand-new explanations. fileciteturn1file0

Use this structure:

**PITCH**

**Pillars**
1. Revenue Leaks  
2. Retention + Memberships  
3. Conversion + Follow-Up Systems  

After each pillar, check in:
“Tracking with me so far?”  
“Does that feel like the missing piece right now?”

**Temperature Check**
“So based on everything we just walked through, how are you feeling about the strategy to get Luxora from where you are now to [goal]?”

If lukewarm:
“What part still feels unclear or incomplete?”

Do **not** move to delivery or price until they are bought in. fileciteturn1file12

**Delivery**
“Cool. So if we partnered up, the focus would be getting the core revenue systems installed quickly: memberships, packages, follow-up, consult conversion, retention, and the client experience. We’re not just trying to get you more leads. We’re fixing the pieces inside the business that turn more opportunities into revenue and make the business less dependent on constant new lead flow.”

“Any questions on how that works before we talk numbers?”

**Price Drop**
“Cool. So to help you [insert goal] over the next [program length], it’s either [payment plan] or a one-time investment of [$___].”

Then stop talking. fileciteturn1file14

Your objection guide should become **post-price loopbacks**. Example:

“Totally fair. Earlier you mentioned poor follow-up and weak membership systems are already costing you revenue every month, so I’m a little confused — is the concern that the investment is too high, or that you’re not fully confident this solves the problem?”

That keeps authority without over-explaining.
